correctness.rationale: The stationary stochastic convolution converges by the Poisson second-moment contraction and has variance 2D/[r(1-a²)]. Conditioning on jumps gives covariance C(t)=2D exp[-r(1-a)|t|]/[r(1-a²)], and its exact Fourier integral gives the stated two-sided S(ω). Maximizing its denominator uses F′=ω²−r²(1-a)(1+3a) and F−2ω²=(1-a)[r²(1-a²)−ω²]; these establish unique interior solutions for |ω|≤r, the exact nonattained infimum for |ω|>r, and one-sided slopes. A compensated jump martingale with bracket 2DT+r(1-a)²∫X² gives the stationary time-average CLT after ergodic averaging and Lindeberg from finite fourth moments. The actual packaged checker passed 53019 finite diagnostics; the proof, not the finite checks, establishes the continuum claim.

value.rationale: The result solves a well-posed continuous optimal-design problem for the complete stationary position-noise spectrum of a natural signed resetting diffusion at fixed rate. The precise change from a unique physical optimal contraction, through exact complete reset at |ω|=r, to a nonattained high-frequency infimum, plus a cusp and a 5/32 long-time averaging variance improvement, give nontrivial structural consequences. Unlike an arbitrary algebraic slice, the frequency and mean-variance observables are motivated by fluctuation measurement; the exact optimizer is not an immediate normalization or known-table reproduction.
